_note: Draft English rendering of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 22, generated by scripts/translate_tafsir_english.py against the JA (not the biblical Hebrew). Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And if the thief be found in the breach, and be struck and killed — take no account of him.
translations.2: And if the sun has shone upon him, then take account of him; and he shall deliver what he stole; and if he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
translations.3: And if the stolen thing be found in his hand — whether ox or donkey or sheep, and they are alive — he shall deliver two in place of the one.
translations.4: And if a man grazes a field or a vineyard of his, and lets his beast loose, and it grazes in another's field — he shall deliver from the best of his field or his vineyard.
translations.5: And if a fire breaks out, and finds thorns and burns a stack, or standing ears of grain, or the rest of what is in the fields — he who kindled the burning shall deliver what is due from him.
translations.6: And if a man entrusts to his fellow silver or vessels to keep for him, and that is stolen from his dwelling — if the thief is found, he shall deliver two.
translations.7: And if the thief is not found, the master of the dwelling shall come forward to the judge, and swear that he did not put forth his hand to his fellow's property.
translations.8: Regarding every matter he denies — whether ox or donkey or sheep or garment or any lost thing — if one says 'this is it,' the matter of the two of them shall be brought before the judge; and whoever the judge finds in the wrong shall deliver two to his fellow.
translations.9: And if a man entrusts to his fellow a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep, or anything of the rest of the beasts, to keep it — and it dies, or is injured, or is taken captive, with no clear witness —
translations.10: an oath by God shall decide between the two of them, that he did not put forth his hand to his fellow's property; and the fellow shall accept it, and he shall deliver nothing.
translations.11: And if it was stolen from his keeping, he shall deliver to him.
translations.12: And if it was torn by a beast, let him bring a witness — and he shall not be liable for the torn animal.
translations.13: And if a man borrows something from his fellow and it is broken or dies, and its owner was not with him — he shall pay a penalty for it.
translations.14: And if its owner was with him, he shall not pay a penalty; and if it was hired, it has already passed with its hire.
translations.15: And if a man deceives a maiden who is a virgin, who has not yet been betrothed, and lies with her — he shall pay her bride-price, and she shall be his wife.
translations.16: And if her father refuses to give her to him in marriage, he shall weigh out for him in silver the bride-price of virgins.
translations.17: And the sorceress — do not let her live.
translations.18: And whoever lies with any of the beasts shall be put to death.
translations.19: And whoever slaughters to the worshipped ones shall be destroyed — except to the name of God alone.
translations.20: And the stranger — do not cheat him nor press him; for how long you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
translations.21: Every widow and orphan — do not wrong them.
translations.22: For if you wrong him, and he cries out to Me — I shall answer him regarding his cry.
translations.23: My anger shall intensify, and I shall kill you by the sword; and your wives shall become widows, and your sons orphans.
translations.24: And if you lend silver to some of My people — to the poor one who is with you — do not be to him like a creditor, and do not impose upon him interest.
translations.25: And if you take your fellow's garment as a pledge, return it to him at the setting of the sun.
translations.26: For it is his only covering — it is the garment of his body — with what shall he lie down? And if he cries out to Me, I shall hear him, for I am compassionate.
translations.27: Do not revile a judge; and a noble among your people — do not curse him.
translations.28: Your first-pressed yield and your first-drip offering — do not delay them; the firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me.
translations.29: So shall you do with your cattle and your flock: it shall remain seven days with its mother, and on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
translations.30: And be for Me a people who are consecrated. And an animal torn in the open country — do not eat it; but throw it to the dog.
